title: LOUISVILLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Louisville Village Board approved a tax levy increase of 4.13%.

During Thursday night’s meeting, trustees passed the tax levy hike with only Trustee Scott Ikemire voting no.  Ikemire did not comment on his vote.  Meanwhile, Trustee Chuck Smith noted that the village needs to make changes to its gas, water, and sewer rates, pointing to those utilities as problem areas.

In financial news, Krista McLaren of Kemper CPA presented the fiscal year 2026 audit, reporting a clean audit with only minor adjustments.  The board also unanimously approved a 3.39% increase for its Snedeker Insurance renewal, voted to renew a 500-thousand-dollar certificate of deposit, and approved leasing the Community Center to Cruse Restaurant for $250 a month.  Village employees will also see a little extra holiday cheer, as trustees approved Christmas bonuses of $350 for full-time staff and $250 for part-time workers.  The board also adjusted the 2027 holiday schedule since Christmas falls on a Saturday next year.

In zoning matters, resident Ben Jordan asked the board for permission to place a refurbished 1997 manufactured home for his daughter on his 1.38-acre property at 910 West Chestnut.  Jordan told the board the home will get new siding, flooring, a furnace, and a water heater, along with separate utility meters.  Trustee Chuck Smith opposed the request, noting the board had denied similar requests for older manufactured homes during his time as mayor.  However, the rest of the board approved the request, contingent on a final inspection.

Finally, Mayor Chris Rinehart is reminding residents about “Christmas in the Village” coming up on Sunday, November 29th, from 3 to 8 pm.  The event features 28 stops around the square, complete with a live Nativity, bell choir performances, a community tree lighting, carriage and kiddie train rides, movies, and a visit from Santa and Mrs. Claus.

title: NORTH WAYNE BOARD MEETING
full_story:
Board members approved a personal leave and dock day requests, and FMLA leave for one employee.  An overnight trip for three Cisne High School FFA students to attend the BUILD Conference in Bloomington-Normal on November 23rd and 24th.  And accepted a $1,000 donation to Cisne High School FFA from the Wayne County Farm Bureau.

Board members also tentatively approved the tax levy and scheduled a Truth in Taxation hearing.  That hearing will be held Wednesday, December 16th, at 4:45 pm at Cisne Middle School, with the regular board meeting following at 5 pm.

The board entered executive session but took no action upon returning.

title: SCOUTING FOR FOOD
full_story:
Tomorrow is pick up day for the Flora Boy Scout Troop 8282 and Louisville Cub Scout Pack 295 “Scouting for Food” annual nonperishable food collection.

If you would like to provide nonperishable food items, please place those items in the blue bags that the boy scouts distributed last Saturday.  If you did not receive a bag or need additional bags you can place items in other bags or boxes and place those on your front porch for pickup tomorrow.

The food collected will be taken to the Clay County food pantry for their normal distribution.

The Boy Scouts will be selling Christmas Trees again this year.  Starting one week from today the scouts will be set up at Dickeys Rentals across from Napa.  The scouts will only have around 50 trees this year, so don’t wait.  The scouts will also be selling homemade baked goods during the tree sales while supplies last.  Proceeds will help send the scouts to Philmont Scout Ranch in 2027.

title: BEST CHRISTMAS LIGHTS IN TOWN CONTEST
full_story:
The City of Flora is getting ready to brighten up the holiday season, and local officials are making a few changes to this year’s annual “Best Christmas Lights in Town” contest.

The city is moving up both the registration deadline and the judging period.  They say the earlier schedule gives them time to compile a list of participating homes so the whole community can drive around, enjoy the displays, and even cast a vote for their favorites.

If you’d like to enter your home, pick up an application at Flora City Hall and once completed, drop it off at city hall by 4:00pm on Friday, December 4th.  Judges tour from 7:00-10:00 pm on December 14th through 17th.  The city announces the winners at the December 21st City Council meeting, and they ask that all participants keep their displays lit through January 1st.

Top decorators will earn a break on their winter utility bill.  First place takes home a 150-dollar utility credit, second place wins a100-dollar bill credit, and third place gets a 75-dollar credit which will apply directly to their February 2027 utility bills.  Please note that city employees are not eligible to enter.

title: GOZIA APPOINTED
full_story:
Justice David K. Overstreet and the Illinois Supreme Court announced the appointment of Judge Wesley A. Gozia as Marion County Resident Circuit Judge in the Fourth Judicial Circuit.

Judge Gozia was appointed to fill the vacancy created by the retirement of Judge Mark W. Stedelin.  The appointment of Mr. Gozia is effective January 1st, and will conclude on December 4th, 2028, following the November 2028 general election.

Judge Gozia was first appointed to the bench in March 2025 to fill a vacancy as an at-large Circuit Judge in the Fourth Judicial Circuit to expire on December 7th.  He previously worked as a sole practitioner at Gozia Law Firm LLC from 2010 to 2025 with a focus on family law, criminal defense, real estate and estate planning.  From 2014 to 2022 he served as a conflict public defender contract attorney for Clinton County where he provided public defense services to indigent clients and brought cases to jury trial.  Since 2023 Judge Gozia has served on the Illinois Supreme Court Executive Committee on the Practice of Law.

“I thank the Supreme Court of Illinois for their confidence in me to allow me to continue serving my community as a circuit judge,” Judge Gozia said.  “I look forward to this new position as Resident Circuit Judge to take on the additional administrative responsibilities to better serve the users of the court system in Marion County.”

Judge Gozia earned his Bachelor of Science from St. Louis University and earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Missouri School of Law.

His professional affiliations include the Clinton County Bar Association, where he has served as President, and the Illinois State Bar Association, where he is a past Secretary and Treasurer.  He is a past member of the ISBA’s Family Law Section Council as well as the Standing Committee on Legal Technology, where he served both as Chair and currently is a member of the ISBA’s Bench and Bar Section Council.

title: FMH ANTIQUE ANGEL TREE
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital’s Senior Life Solutions Department is spreading holiday cheer through its annual Antique Christmas Angel Tree, helping older adults throughout the community who may be in need or do not have family nearby.

Each ornament on the Antique Christmas Angel Tree represents an older adult and includes their name along with a list of items they would like or need this holiday season.  Gifts may include simple necessities such as warm blankets, socks and other thoughtful items that can bring comfort and joy during the colder months.

Community members are invited to sponsor an “antique angel” by selecting an ornament from the tree.  Those interested in participating can contact FMH Senior Life Solutions at 618-847-8298 to choose an ornament and learn more about the program.

All gifts should be wrapped and delivered to the Senior Life Solutions Department at Fairfield Memorial Hospital no later than Friday, December 4th.

Through this special holiday project, Senior Life Solutions hopes to remind older adults in the community that they are remembered, valued and cared for.

For more information or to sponsor an angel, contact FMH Senior Life Solutions at 618-847-8298.

title: THANKSGIVING DINNER
full_story:
Thanksgiving dinner will cost more than the previous four years as a result of higher fuel and production costs.  But it still remains below the 2022 record.

The American Farm Bureau Federation’s (AFBF) 41st annual Thanksgiving Dinner Cost Survey found a classic feast for 10 is $58.63 or $5.86 per person, up more than 6% from 2025.  Still, the 2026 cost remains 8.5% lower than the record-high year in 2022.

In Illinois, the classic meal was forecasted to average $56.89, with the Midwest cost achieving the second-most affordable status in the nation after the South at $54.33, and ahead of the West, at $58.74, and the Northeast at $61.57.

“We recognize that higher grocery prices continue to put pressure on Illinois families, especially during the holidays,” said Illinois Farm Bureau President Philip Nelson.  “Farmers are feeling those financial pressures, too, as the costs of fuel, fertilizer, labor and other essential inputs remain high.  But farmers don’t set the prices consumers pay at the grocery store, nor can they simply raise the prices they receive for their products to offset higher production costs.

Turkey held the 2026 slot for the largest increase of price with an average cost of $23.68 for a 16-pound frozen turkey, up 10% from last year.

However, Farm Bureau volunteers checked prices the first week of November, before most grocery stores began offering discounts and specials for turkeys.  The average per-pound feature price for whole frozen turkeys declined during the second week of November, according to recent USDA Ag Marketing Service data.

AFBF credits increased production costs and a recovering turkey population among reasons for the price increase.

The AFBF Thanksgiving dinner survey was first conducted in 1986.  The informal survey provides a record of comparative holiday meal costs over the years.  Farm Bureau’s classic survey menu has remained unchanged since 1986 to allow for consistent price comparisons.

The survey shopping list includes turkey, stuffing, sweet potatoes, rolls, peas, cranberries, a veggie tray and pumpkin pie with whipped cream, all in quantities sufficient for 10 servings.

And while the overall costs saw an increase, a third of the ingredients surveyed declined in price, including the veggie tray, frozen pie crusts, frozen green peas and whipping cream.

Low wheat prices aided in bringing down the cost of some items that require flour, while the explanation for veggie tray items such as carrots and celery may be due to a rebound from past shortages caused by severe weather and disease, AFBF stated.

On the other hand, cranberries, dinner rolls and whole milk all increased in price, with cranberries up 8.8%, whole milk up 8.6% and dinner rolls up 7%.

The Farm Bureau price survey also included an expanded menu of boneless ham, russet potatoes and frozen green beans.  Adding those foods to the classic Thanksgiving menu increases the overall cost by $23.09, to a total of $81.72.
